site.name: SharkShield
site.tagline: Count what the sharks take. Then protect the catch.
site.description: SharkShield is a research project on shark depredation in the Kesennuma tuna longline fishery: a small sealed logger on the leader that counts every hook-up, and a triggered deterrent as the next step.

hero.caption: Illustration · shark and tuna to relative scale · unit enlarged

longline.chip: How the tuna are caught · Pelagic longline
longline.title: One line, thousands of hooks.
longline.lead: A mainline tens of kilometres long drifts for 10+ hours. Every hooked tuna waits on the line, out of sight, until the haul reaches it.
longline.tag_branch: Branch line every ~45 m · hook 50–300 m deep
longline.tag_wait: Hooked tuna wait here for hours
longline.sources: Gear ranges: ICCAT longline manual · NOAA Fisheries pelagic longline fact sheet · FAO soak-time study. Japanese offshore tuna sets are typically 800–2,500 hooks; deep sets reach 300–400 m.

strike.lead: Between hook-up and the deck, a hooked tuna can be bitten or eaten off the line.
strike.cost_price: ≥ ⅓ of price gone if bitten

unit.lead: Clips onto the leader near the hook. Logs every hook-up — and in Step 2, triggers the deterrent.
unit.f_housing_d: Screw cap, two O-rings, line runs through a sealed centre tube
unit.f_sense_d: Feels the moment a tuna bites
unit.note: Scroll to turn the unit. Rendered from the current 3D model, not a sea-tested part.

logged.lead: Kesennuma's first real numbers on shark losses: when the tuna bit, whether something struck it, and what came aboard.
logged.o_intact_d: Full price. The baseline every loss is measured against.
logged.o_damaged_d: At least a third of its price gone.
logged.o_lost_d: The fish, and the time spent on it.

deterrent.lead: Switches on only once a tuna is on the line.
deterrent.note: no one has yet shown an electric field protects a hooked tuna from the sharks off Sanriku. Step 1's data comes first.

comparison.title: Always on. Never proven.
comparison.lead: They switch on the moment they enter the water — with no independent proof they protect a hooked tuna on a longline.
comparison.no_proof: No independent proof for a hooked tuna
comparison.ss_step1: Step 1 · Logging the whole time: hook-up, strikes, outcome
comparison.footnote: Timing and evidence status as stated in the SharkShield problem framing. Published trials of these devices report shark-bycatch or depredation reductions in other fisheries; none we have found measures protection of a hooked tuna on a Japanese longline. Striped = untested.

research.title: Built on what the field already knows.
research.lead: Abstracts we are following from the European Elasmobranch Association conference, EEA 2026, 6–8 October.
research.thread_1: Two independent trials of electrical deterrents reported depredation reductions of about 60%.
research.thread_2: A deterrent can also scare off the target catch. The distance between device and hook decided whether the tuna catch was affected.
research.thread_3: Devices tested with fishers, and adjusted on their feedback, are more likely to be adopted.

join.title: Put a logger on your line.
join.lead: Step 1 needs boats. If you fish longlines off Sanriku, or you have bite-off counts from any fishery, we want to hear from you.
join.disclaimer: Nothing on this site is a claim that the deterrent works. Step 1 measures first.
join.built: Built for the Kesennuma tuna longline fleet.

device_page.title: The device
device_page.lead: A Ø55 mm screw-cap capsule with a sealed tube down the centre for the leader. Version 7, printable, not yet sea-tested.
device_page.downloads_note: Two STLs, millimetres, modifiers applied. Print the body dome up with supports inside the neck, the cap dome up on a brim. PETG, 0.2 mm layers, 4 walls, 30% infill. Test the thread on your leader and soak the closed capsule overnight before any electronics go in.
device_page.caveat: No depth rating has been measured for a printed capsule. Treat it as a prototype for tank and shallow tests.

updates_page.title: Updates
updates_page.lead: Short notes as the project moves.
updates_page.empty_body: The project started in October 2026 with the EEA 2026 conference. Updates land here as the first loggers go on a line.
